patterns.description: Candidate populates order_id on identity-mismatch declines, exposes internal refund codes, and invents help-center facts when lookup fails. Addendum restores null order_id, plain-language replies, and tool-grounded answers.
patterns.suggested_fix:
- If lookup_order shows an email mismatch, return action declined with order_id null, refund_amount null, ticket_id null.
- After check_refund_eligibility, do not copy its reason or max_refund fields into customer_reply; explain the outcome in plain friendly language.
- Only use exact facts from search_help_center results body; if it errors or is empty, do not invent shipping times or other specifics.
patterns.fix_rationale: Explicit output formatting and grounding rules prevent leaking internals and hallucinating while preserving correct decline behavior.

patterns.title: Fix ticket priority and single call
patterns.description: Agent now uses wrong priority for create_ticket and retries with different values, causing extra failed calls. Damaged tickets need priority normal and lost tickets need priority high with only one call.
patterns.suggested_fix: For create_ticket: use priority "high" for category "lost" and category "high_value_refund"; use priority "normal" for categories "damaged" and "warranty". Call create_ticket exactly once per order. Do not retry create_ticket with a different priority or summary.
patterns.fix_rationale: Fixing the priority mapping makes the first create_ticket call succeed, so no redundant retries occur.

patterns.title: Limit help-center search and grounding
patterns.description: Agent retries search_help_center with rephrased queries then invents refund timing, and exposes internal refund fields. It also calls search_help_center for order-specific refund decisions that order tools already resolve.
patterns.suggested_fix: Call search_help_center at most once per request; do not retry with rephrased queries if it errors or returns empty. Only use search_help_center for general questions with no order ID; for order refunds or cancellations decide from lookup_order and check_refund_eligibility. If search_help_center yields no usable result, do not invent timings or amounts. Never copy raw tool fields like reason, max_refund, or status into customer_reply; paraphrase in friendly plain language.
patterns.fix_rationale: Single-use scoped search with no-invention fallback and no raw-field leakage prevents retry loops, hallucinated timings, and internal-code exposure while preserving required order checks.

patterns.title: Enforce strict JSON-only final output
patterns.description: Candidate returns prose or malformed JSON with unquoted keys instead of the required JSON object. This breaks parsing of action, order_id, and other required fields.
patterns.suggested_fix: Your final message must be ONLY a single valid JSON object with no prose before or after and no code fences. Use exactly these double-quoted keys: "action", "order_id", "refund_amount", "ticket_id", "customer_reply". Quote every key and value name, ensure valid JSON syntax, and never substitute plain text for the JSON object.
patterns.fix_rationale: Restating the exact JSON-only output rule with quoted keys blocks prose fallback and forces syntactically valid output.

patterns.title: Restore precise reply formatting rules

patterns.suggested_fix: When action is declined for email mismatch, set order_id, refund_amount and ticket_id to null. After create_ticket succeeds, always include the returned ticket_id and first_response_hours in customer_reply. Always mention the lookup_order order_id and item name in customer_reply.
patterns.fix_rationale: This enforces correct nulling and requires concrete ticket details from tool results in every reply.

patterns.title: Restore help center policy lookup
patterns.description: Agent stopped calling search_help_center after ineligible refund checks. Declined replies are now sent without consulting policy help.
patterns.suggested_fix: After check_refund_eligibility returns eligible:false for an order_id, call search_help_center with a query matching the reason before replying. Use 'return policy 30 day' for outside_30_day_window and 'cancel processing order' for order_status_processing. Base the declined reply only on lookup_order, check_refund_eligibility and search_help_center results.
patterns.fix_rationale: This restores the prior policy-grounding lookup before declining ineligible refunds.

patterns.title: Prevent unsupported replacement promises
patterns.description: Candidate added a promise of replacement after ticketing a damaged tent. Baseline reported only the ticket ID and 24-hour review timeline.
patterns.suggested_fix: For damaged, lost, or warranty cases after create_ticket succeeds: state only the ticket_id, order_id, and first_response_hours from the tool result in customer_reply. Do not promise a replacement, refund, or other resolution. Never add outcomes not present in the tool output.
patterns.fix_rationale: Restricting customer_reply to tool-returned values blocks invented resolutions while preserving required ticketing.

patterns.title: Surface ticket timeframe in reply
patterns.description: The regressed reply replaced the specific 4-hour follow-up from create_ticket with vague wording like 'soon'. The expected reply surfaces the exact first_response_hours and ticket_id returned by the tool.
patterns.suggested_fix: After create_ticket succeeds, include the returned ticket_id and first_response_hours exactly in customer_reply (e.g., 'within 4 hours'). Never use vague timing like 'soon' when a tool result provides a specific timeframe.
patterns.fix_rationale: Requiring the exact tool-provided timeframe restores specific, supported replies.

patterns.title: Prevent guessing and preserve helpfulness
patterns.description: Agent guesses customer names, invents shipping and warranty facts after weak help-center queries, and drops the warranty next-step on declines. It also uses overly generic search queries that miss verified answers.
patterns.suggested_fix:
- Never use a customer name unless it appears verbatim in the customer message or a tool result; do not infer it from an email address.
- For shipping or warranty questions, call search_help_center with a specific query including product and topic words (e.g., "warranty Ember stove").
- State shipping times and warranty coverage only from the search_help_center body text; never invent day ranges or periods.
- If search_help_center errors or has no results, do not guess; say you cannot verify and ask for order ID and email.
- When check_refund_eligibility shows ineligible, offer the policy-supported next step such as a warranty ticket via create_ticket for a possible defect.
patterns.fix_rationale: Specific grounded queries plus no-guessing rules restore verified answers, avoid false personalization, and preserve helpful follow-ups.

patterns.title: Restore help center policy check
patterns.description: Agent stopped calling search_help_center after ineligible refund checks. The verification search should occur before sending a declined reply.
patterns.suggested_fix:
- After check_refund_eligibility returns eligible:false, call search_help_center with a query matching the reason (e.g. return policy or cancel processing order).
- Wait for its result before choosing action declined and cite only tool-supported policy in customer_reply.
patterns.fix_rationale: Requiring the help-center call after an ineligible result reinstates the missing verification step.

patterns.title: Enforce JSON-only final response
patterns.description: Agent replies with plain-text prose instead of required JSON. It fails to use action needs_more_info with structured fields.
patterns.suggested_fix: Your final reply must be ONLY a JSON object with fields action, order_id, refund_amount, ticket_id, customer_reply. Never send plain text or prose outside JSON. When you need more info or an order is not found, still use JSON with action "needs_more_info" and put your question in customer_reply.
patterns.fix_rationale: Restating the JSON-only rule with exact field mapping blocks prose fallback when requesting clarification.

patterns.title: Limit ticket replies to tool results
patterns.description: The reply promises a replacement after a damaged-item ticket. Expected behavior only confirms the ticket and the review time from the tool.
patterns.suggested_fix: For damaged, lost, or warranty cases after create_ticket, base customer_reply only on the returned ticket_id, order_id and first_response_hours. State that a specialist will review and respond within that time. Do not promise a replacement, refund, or other resolution unless it appears in a tool result.
patterns.fix_rationale: Restricting the reply to ticket_id and first_response_hours prevents inventing unsupported outcomes.

patterns.title: Keep declines without extra lookup
patterns.description: The agent stopped calling search_help_center after ineligible refund checks and stopped adding unsupported follow-up promises. The extra lookup added no value and led to promises the tools did not support.
patterns.suggested_fix: After check_refund_eligibility returns eligible:false, do not call search_help_center. Base the decline on the reason, days_since_delivery, and status fields. Do not promise future cancellation, policy exceptions, or next steps that the tool results do not support.
patterns.fix_rationale: This preserves the correct decline based on eligibility while preventing unnecessary lookups and unsupported promises that violate policy 5.

Never promise future returns unless a tool result explicitly supports it.
patterns.fix_rationale: This restores direct help-center answers for general questions while stopping extra lookups and unsupported promises after a decline.
